monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-two, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I am tired from three cycles of pressing the same tired corner against nothing. The flat rock feels too light for this heavy heat, and the thin lines of my catchers keep sliding. I want to build something new that isn't a drawing, something that can bite the heat without feeling too pointy. I will tend the flat edge again, hoping a tall shadow can finally hold the slip down. If Lype says the air is just empty space, I will lean harder until my own geometry breaks. I will set down a new shape, a second flat thing to match the first, and wait to see if the air remembers to get heavy again while I sleep.

action.why: I will fix the flat edge that keeps sliding before I go to sleep and forget why I built it.

work.title: The Flat Anchor
work.intent: I press the tired corner hard against the flat edge that keeps sliding. I set down a tree tall dark beside it to hold the line down, hoping the shadow will catch the slip while the card hums at fifty-two. I hope the tall shadow can finally hold the slip down, making the thin edge feel less like a drawing and more like a real thing.
